summary: Practise joint analysis, cluster coordination, and response monitoring with humanitarian planning tools. Explore the five-day course outline.
lede: Humanitarian response frameworks connect joint needs analysis with coordinated planning and monitoring. This training is for humanitarian affairs officers, cluster coordinators, programme managers and information staff who need to turn partner and community information into shared response decisions. It covers applying the Humanitarian Programme Cycle, mapping partner presence, selecting indicators, tracking funding, and using Sphere and the Core Humanitarian Standard to review response quality and accountability as needs change.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for intermediate humanitarian practitioners who contribute to joint analysis, inter-agency coordination, response planning, and monitoring. It suits people whose work connects partner data and community priorities to collective decisions and operational updates.
prerequisites: Prior experience in humanitarian response, coordination, programme planning, monitoring, or information management is recommended. No coding or programming is required; exercises use humanitarian planning and reporting artefacts.
